topics.topic: Precedence and lexical behavior of request depth checks on malformed input
questions: When the raw request is both malformed JSON and appears to exceed the depth ceiling, what exact lexical rules does the pre-parse measurement apply, and which failure is considered first?
If text is malformed JSON and also contains nesting beyond json_depth_max, does the depth check fail first, does malformed syntax prevent a depth result, and what refusal detail is returned?
How is the pre-parse depth check classified and ordered when the request is malformed, has unbalanced delimiters, invalid escaping or invalid UTF-8?

judgement.why: This asks the same malformed-input depth-ordering question already decided by P3, and its deciding later-state passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Precedence between malformed-JSON and request-depth failures
quotes: canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1) and is neither held exactly by an IEEE double nor written exactly as that double's ECMAScript shortest round-trip form — 100000000000000000000, which a double holds exactly, and 18014398509481990, the form JCS writes for 1.801439850948199e+16, are each that double, so canonical bytes always parse again to the same bytes —, when the value nests deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, the depth of a scalar being 0 and of an array or object one more than its deepest element or member value, a member's name adding no level, 1 when it has none, found while parsing and never by a recursion deeper than that constant, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.

answer_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] After the token check, before any other bound is checked and before the message is parsed, walked or canonicalised, the depth of the request message as received, as canonical_bytes defines depth, MUST be within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, measured on the message text without recursion, else invalid_request; a deeper request never reaches a recursive walk. Each JSON text the message carries as a string is measured on its own by canonical_bytes, so the message around it adds no depth to it. Request bounds, each counted as UTF-8 bytes of the field as received: implementation code within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_IMPLEMENTATION_CODE_BYTES_MAX constant; the json_text of a trial case input or expected output, of a flow constant and of a run input within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant; the decoded bytes of a trial case file within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant; every other string anywhere in the request within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant; a page_size given below 1 or above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_PAGE_SIZE_MAX constant; base64 text that does not decode; each a failure answered invalid_request (A16 rules 4 and 6).
precedent.why: The later notes require a non-recursive pre-parse depth scan and make the first offending item in text order decide malformed-versus-depth failures.

topics.topic: Serialization boundary and unit used for function-output depth checks
questions: What exact byte text is depth-scanned and counted when a Python output cannot be canonicalized, and where is that text produced without first recursively walking the returned Python object?
Is the returned dict as a whole also depth-bounded, or only each member value after the runner has inspected the dict and selected the declared output entries?
What exact serialization crosses the sandbox boundary, and is depth measured on each serialized port value or on the returned output dictionary as a whole?

At what exact boundary is each Python output converted to a JSON text and depth-checked, and how are cyclic objects, shared references, custom objects or objects that trigger recursion during traversal classified without first walking them?

judgement.why: This repeats P2's question about function-output serialization, per-output depth measurement, noncanonical output counting and outcome precedence.

precedent.topic: Function-output serialization, depth measurement, and validation precedence
quotes: runner_source: [BEHAVIOR] When run returned, the program MUST write one returned message: whether the value is a dict with only str keys and, for each key, its form — json for a value port whose value json.dumps accepts with sort_keys=True, separators (',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False and allow_nan=False (for a many value port, a list), file for a file port whose value is bytes, file_list for a many file port whose value is a list of bytes, not_representable otherwise and for a key that is no output port. Before it builds that message it MUST pre-count the representable outputs against output_bytes — each value output as the UTF-8 bytes of that json.dumps, each file as its bytes — and when the pre-count exceeds output_bytes write a resource hit and no outputs; a MemoryError while it pre-counts, encodes or writes the outputs is a resource hit too, so an output too large to send concludes resource_exhausted rather than crashed. It writes nothing to standard output or standard error.

judge_execution: [BEHAVIOR] MUST decide from the observation, the output ports and the bounds it is given and the release constants it imports, nothing else, and run nothing. The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output — for an output whose JSON text canonical_bytes refuses, the UTF-8 bytes of that text as returned — and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated. A bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it — the report's resource_hit, the observation's channel_over_bound or that count over bounds.output_bytes; the parent kills an environment only for its wall deadline (owner, 2026-10-06) and for its channel bound, which execute_function observes as channel_over_bound.

judge_execution: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] When cleanup was confirmed the outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the report's resource_hit is true — the runner hit its memory, process or scratch limit, the scratch limit being the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant, which runner_arguments writes as file_size_limit into the runner's command line and which is no field of ResourceBounds or RunnerLaunch —, the observation's channel_over_bound holds, or the output count exceeds bounds.output_bytes; sandbox_violation when the report holds any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the report says crashed, the runner exited abnormally, or no returned message was read — the report's returned is None: read_runner_report always gives a RunnerReport, for a channel that carried nothing one with no trap hit, no resource hit, crashed false, failure None and returned None, so the observation always holds a report; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value and spool ceilings are applied by the module that stores or spools an output.
precedent.why: The later notes specify the exact json.dumps representation, safe handling of unserialisable and memory-exhausting values, parent-side canonicalization and counting, and the complete outcome precedence.

topics.topic: Which request fields carry native JSON versus embedded JSON text
questions: Are values, constants, schemas and guard values represented on the surface as strings containing JSON texts, or as native nested JSON values in the request message?
Which request fields contain nested JSON values directly and which contain strings that must themselves be parsed as JSON?
Which request fields contain embedded JSON text strings, which contain direct JSON values, and is the list of value, constant, schema and guard value exhaustive?

judgement.why: This repeats P4's question about JSON-text string fields and their relationship to the enclosing request message.

precedent.topic: Representation of carried JSON fields and interaction with whole-request depth
quotes: answer_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] After the token check, before any other bound is checked and before the message is parsed, walked or canonicalised, the depth of the request message as received, as canonical_bytes defines depth, MUST be within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, measured on the message text without recursion, else invalid_request; a deeper request never reaches a recursive walk. Each JSON text the message carries as a string is measured on its own by canonical_bytes, so the message around it adds no depth to it. Request bounds, each counted as UTF-8 bytes of the field as received: implementation code within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_IMPLEMENTATION_CODE_BYTES_MAX constant; the json_text of a trial case input or expected output, of a flow constant and of a run input within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant; the decoded bytes of a trial case file within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant; every other string anywhere in the request within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant; a page_size given below 1 or above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_PAGE_SIZE_MAX constant; base64 text that does not decode; each a failure answered invalid_request (A16 rules 4 and 6).

answer_request: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] As part of the fit check, before the actor check and before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1).

handle_start_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST turn each RequestJsonValue into a JsonPayload of the same port with its canonical JSON bytes, call start_run with the flow_id, those inputs and the actor, and show the RunAnswer it returns as a ShownRun.
precedent.why: The later surface text makes values, constants, schemas and guard values JSON-text string fields and measures each independently from the enclosing JSON-RPC message.

topics.topic: Boundary of the outer request value subject to the depth ceiling
questions: Which bytes constitute the JSON text whose request-message depth is measured: the complete MCP/JSON-RPC envelope, the operation invocation object, or only its arguments object?
What exact JSON value is the request message whose whole depth is compared with json_depth_max?

judgement.why: This repeats P9's question about the exact outer request boundary whose depth is measured.

precedent.topic: Request-message boundary used for depth measurement
quotes: serve_kernel: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read at most one byte more of a request body than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant allows, so an oversized request still reaches answer_request and is refused there; when answer_request raises StopRequiredError or any other failure it let propagate because its answer is internal_error, MUST first send that request the internal_error answer built by translate_failure, without detail, and then end the process with a non-zero exit code, so the next start derives every run that has not ended (A03 rule 7, A14 rules 5 and 7).

answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, parsed only after the depth check, which follows the size and token checks. A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing. A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.
precedent.why: The later surface text identifies the measured input as the HTTP request-body bytes containing the complete JSON-RPC message, before that message is parsed.

topics.topic: Canonical storage and downstream representation of embedded JSON text
questions: What representation is passed to operation checks and persisted after an embedded JSON string is validated and canonicalized?
Are JSON-text request fields an explicit exception to the verbatim-text rule, and does the kernel retain only canonical bytes or both the submitted text and its canonical form?

quotes: answer_request: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] As part of the fit check, before the actor check and before any handler runs, MUST replace every JSON text the request carries — the json_text of each RequestJsonValue and RequestConstant, the value_schema of every Port and RequestConstant, the guard_value of every EdgeGuard — by its canonical form obtained from canonical_bytes; a NonCanonicalValueError there is invalid_request, so modules below receive only canonical JSON (A01 rule 1).

handle_add_trial_case: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST turn each RequestPayload into a PortPayload of the same port: RequestJsonValue to JsonPayload with the canonical JSON bytes, RequestFile to FilePayload with the base64-decoded bytes, RequestFileList to FileListPayload with each element decoded, in list order; expected_outputs absent stays absent.

handle_compose_flow_version: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST turn each RequestConstant into a ConstantInput with the same to_node, to_port, canonical value_schema text and disclosure_class and with canonical_json set to the canonical bytes of its json_text.

answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] Text an agent supplies — purposes, implementation code, names — is data: it is never evaluated, imported, compiled, formatted or interpreted in the kernel process; a JSON text it supplies is data too, parsed only as JSON by canonical_bytes and by the schema check of the module that judges it, never evaluated or executed; no answer and no refusal carries a token, a service credential, a host path or a stack trace, an internal error included (A16 rules 5 and 7).
judgement.why: The later notes require canonical replacement before handlers, pass values onward as canonical bytes and schema facts as canonical text, and expressly distinguish JSON parsing from evaluating agent text.

topics.topic: Installation configuration JSON format and depth-validation rules

Is the installation configuration file required to be one JSON document, and what decoding, duplicate-key and top-level-shape rules apply before its depth can be measured?

judgement.why: The installation file's serialization, decoding, duplicate-member treatment and exact top-level shape are format and schema questions owned by State 6, not State 2 rule closure.

topics.topic: Treatment of previously stored deep values after the depth ceiling is lowered
questions: After an upgrade lowers json_depth_max, what happens when an old stored constant or value is passed through a function or service and re-enters as a newly produced output deeper than the new limit?

After a release lowers the ceiling, what happens when an old over-limit StoredValue is echoed by a function, incorporated into a newly assembled mapped list, or produced again with bytes equal to the existing stored value?

judgement.why: This repeats P1's question about applying the running release's depth ceiling when old values re-enter as newly produced outputs or mapped lists.

precedent.topic: Depth limit governing newly produced outputs in older executions or from older values
quotes: judge_execution: [BEHAVIOR] MUST decide from the observation, the output ports and the bounds it is given and the release constants it imports, nothing else, and run nothing. The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output — for an output whose JSON text canonical_bytes refuses, the UTF-8 bytes of that text as returned — and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated. A bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it — the report's resource_hit, the observation's channel_over_bound or that count over bounds.output_bytes; the parent kills an environment only for its wall deadline (owner, 2026-10-06) and for its channel bound, which execute_function observes as channel_over_bound.

send_prepared_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] A 2xx answer with value output ports must be UTF-8 text parsing as one JSON object without duplicate member names, whatever its Content-Type, whose depth, as canonical_bytes defines depth, measured on the body as a whole without recursion before it is parsed, is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant; each output port takes the member of the same name, which must exist and fit the port by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant as size bound, so that a value's own size is judged only by the value_too_large check below, members no port names are ignored, and any failure is contract_violation; after everything else fits, a value whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant is contract_violation with detail value_too_large.

assemble_mapped_lists: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST measure every value list against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant before it answers anything, and when the canonical bytes of any exceed it, or canonical_bytes refuses the list with NonCanonicalValueError — which for a list of stored canonical values happens only when it nests deeper than the release depth ceiling —, answer ListsOverCeiling naming the node and the first such port in the order given, with no list; it is given only the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output, so every delivered list of a node is measured before any of them is written or delivered.
precedent.why: The later behavior notes apply the running release's imported depth ceiling to every newly produced function output, service response, and assembled mapped list, regardless of the age of its inputs or pinned records.
